info.title: LISA External API
info.description: Versioned contract for the REST and SSE surfaces shared by the TypeScript server and native clients. Version 1 preserves the existing response bodies; additive optional fields are backwards compatible.

200.description: Normalized sessions from every enabled observer.
Retained LISA-owned dispatches.
One retained dispatch plus its bounded output tail.
Lightweight current LISA state.
Newline-delimited SSE data frames. Unknown event types and additive fields must be ignored.
Chat events using the shared SSE event envelope.
Lisa's own chat sessions on disk, newest first (PLAN_UI_SESSION_SHELL_v1.1). The on-disk file path is server-internal and never serialized.
Creates a fresh Lisa session and makes it the active web session.
Switches the active web session to an existing one.

The caller's reach-out controls (docs/POLICY_REACH_OUT.md): proactivity dial, per-source switches, quiet hours, channels, plus today's unsolicited budget. Scoped to the signed-in account in the cloud edition.
Merges the patch over the stored settings and returns the new view. Unknown fields and invalid values are rejected, not ignored.
Aggregates of the reach-out ledger for the last N local days: delivered / deferred / dropped per source and the useful rate. Never returns ledger rows or any message text.
Records the user's verdict on a delivered notice. Feeds the value gate: dismissed kinds push less.
Every task of the signed-in account, oldest first.

200.description: Both memory stores.

200.description: The updated entry (its id changes with its text).
The entry was removed.

post.description: Forget a topic across memory, KB, sessions, reflections, tasks, search indexes, relationships and (literal redactions only) Lisa's journal; the report names every place in the home it did not scan (notScanned). The topic matches as whole words, case-insensitive (exact character sequence for scripts without spaces, see report.match). dryRun: true previews every item that would change, each with an id and a short snippet of the text around the match, plus a digest. Apply by sending the same query with that digest; the server re-plans and answers 409 preview_changed unless the set is exactly the previewed one. An applied report carries no content.

200.description: What was (or would be) forgotten, plus honest residuals.

get.description: Download the caller's Lisa as a gzip'd tar (soul, MEMORY.md, USER.md, kb, skills, tasks, optional sessions) with manifest.json last. Never contains secrets, keys, accounts, devices, billing, warden/ or task leases/locks/outbox. Cloud: the signed-in tenant only; Mac: loopback owner only.

200.description: The archive (Content-Disposition: attachment).

Newest-first summaries of the caller's dream records (one per reflective pass that changed something, saw a reconsider note, or ran while a part could not be captured). `pendingReconsider` counts notes not yet acknowledged. Cloud: scoped to the signed-in account; a cloud caller without an account gets 403.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Server-minted dream id (UTC millisecond stamp + random suffix).

200.description: One full dream record (per-file and per-commit diffs are size-capped) plus the reconsider requests filed against it. A record bigger than the 512 KiB record cap is served trimmed with `readTruncated: true`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Server-minted dream id (UTC millisecond stamp + random suffix).

200.description: Reverts the dream's changes to the user's own data. Memory is reverted entry by entry against the current file (the dream's added entries taken out, its removed entries put back; never a whole pre-dream file). KB pages and skills are restored file by file only when unchanged since the dream (409 `revert_conflict` otherwise, unless `force`). A path that resolves outside its part's directory (a symlink) is a conflict `unsafe_target`. `soul` is refused (400). 403 for a cross-site request, a non-loopback Host on a loopback-trusted caller, or a caller who may not approve (shared token, paired device).

409.description: A selected KB page or skill changed since the dream (`modified_since`), has no pre-dream copy or was also changed outside the pass while it ran (`not_revertible`), or resolves outside its part's directory (`unsafe_target`); or a memory revert would push MEMORY.md / USER.md past the memory store's cap (`memory_full`). Nothing was written. With `force: true`, changed files are overwritten and `not_revertible` / `unsafe_target` files are skipped; `memory_full` is refused even then. Memory never conflicts on content (it reverts entry by entry; see `changedSince` in the 200 response).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Server-minted dream id (UTC millisecond stamp + random suffix).

201.description: Queues the user's note for Lisa's next reflective pass (session reflection or an idle run), which decides for herself. Never edits soul files. A note is acknowledged only when a pass that saw it finishes; a pass that fails or dies puts it back, so it is never lost but may be shown again. 409 `no_soul_changes` when the dream did not touch her soul, 409 `dreams_disabled` when dreams are turned off (LISA_REVE_DREAMS), 429 `queue_full` when 200 notes are already waiting. 403 for a cross-site request, a non-loopback Host on a loopback-trusted caller, or a caller who may not approve (shared token, paired device).

200.description: The caller's reconsider queue: pending, claimed (shown to a pass still running) and delivered (acknowledged by a pass that finished).

Deterministic per-UTC-day sums of the drift indicators every dream carries (identity/purpose/constitution patches, values/opinions churn, desire churn, emotion volatility, memory/KB/skills activity), zero-filled.

ApiVersion.description: Major protocol version of this response.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code in most v1 routes; a few legacy routes still return a short message.

status.description: running | ok (observed exit 0) | failed (non-zero exit or signal) | unknown (not alive, no exit observed). `alive: false` alone does not mean success: the child is detached, so a crash, an OOM kill and a clean finish are indistinguishable from the pid.

exitCode.description: Observed exit code. null when the process died by signal; absent when no exit was ever observed.

exitSignal.description: Signal name when the process died by signal.

exitCode.description: Observed exit code. null when the process died by signal; absent when no exit was ever observed.

exitSignal.description: Signal name when the process died by signal.

SSEEvent.description: Open event envelope. Clients must ignore unknown types and additive fields; known v1 types include agent_session_update, claude_session_update, mood, chat_start, chat_delta, chat_end, idle_message, advisor_suggestions, screen_suggestion, sense_event, reflect_done, approval_requested, approval_resolved, task_updated, task_deleted, task_run_started, task_run_finished, task_result and error. GitHub local preview adds github_connection_changed (sessionId only).

ReachOutSettingsPatch.description: Any subset of ReachOutSettings; nested objects are merged field by field.

expr.description: at:<ISO-8601> | every:<n>(m|h|d) | daily:HH:MM | weekdays:HH:MM | weekly:<mon..sun>@HH:MM | cron:<m h dom mon dow>

tz.description: IANA time zone; the host's zone when omitted.

categories.description: Warden's action categories (read, self, draft, write, exec, network, send, publish, purchase, delete, credential) or the migration's `heartbeat-legacy` label. Any other value (such as the `web` / `mail` labels earlier versions accepted) is dropped on create, edit and load: it pre-approves nothing.

tools.description: Exact tool names the run is offered: printable, no whitespace, at most 199 characters. A task file naming anything else loads switched off; a request naming it is refused.

targets.description: Targets (hosts, paths, repos) a pre-approval is limited to: printable, at most 200 characters. They limit calls whose targets can be listed; a call with none to list (a shell command) is pre-approved on the tools or categories alone when it stays on this machine, and is not pre-approved when it reaches another host.

TaskEnvelope.description: What a task may use. Until the user confirms it (`envelopeConfirmation`), it only restricts the tools a run is offered and pre-approves nothing. Confirmed, it lets the listed tools / categories run without asking — except, in a run that has read outside content, exec, delete, send, publish, network writes and writes outside the task's own workspace, which ask.

digest.description: sha256 of the task's instruction, kind, schedule, trigger, envelope and notify mode. Send it back as `confirmEnvelope` to confirm the task as shown.

confirmed.description: The user confirmed the task as it is now.

preapproves.description: The envelope names a tool or category a confirmation would pre-approve.

summary.description: Plain-words lines to show before asking: the instruction, when it runs, and which actions would run without asking.

maxApprovals.description: How many approvals one run may ask for (default 5). The next ask stops the run with stopReason `approval_limit` instead of waiting, and is not announced.

approvalWaitMs.description: Total time one run may wait for approvals, across its asks and segments (default 60 minutes; at most 6 hours, 15 minutes hosted). Past it the run stops with stopReason `approval_limit`.

digest.description: The task's confirmation digest when the user confirmed it.

mac.description: HMAC of the task id and the digest under the home's Warden key. Only the user's own surface (`lisa tasks enable`, a confirming `PATCH`) can produce it; a confirmation without a valid one counts as unconfirmed.

envelopeConfirmation.description: The user confirmed the envelope as a pre-approval. It counts only while `digest` equals the task's current digest (`TaskConfirmation.digest`) and `mac` verifies; every edit of the title, instruction, schedule, trigger, host, envelope, notify mode or budget, every edit by Lisa's own task tools, and every enable, clears it. Absent: the envelope only restricts.

lastSummaryTainted.description: `lastSummary` was written by a run that had read outside content: the next run quotes it as data and starts tainted.

workspaceTainted.description: A run that had read outside content made state-changing calls with the task's folder writable to it: every later run starts tainted.

stateSeal.description: HMAC, under the home's Warden key, of the task id, `lastSummary`, `lastSummaryTainted` and `workspaceTainted` as the runner last wrote them. Missing or wrong: the summary is read as a tainted run's, and a folder that holds anything as tainted.

pausedReason.description: Why the engine switched the task off by itself. Cleared when the user enables it.

resumeAt.description: The active run is parked after a failed attempt and resumes (same run) at this time.

tokens.description: Tokens processed. The run's token budget is measured against the sum of all four.

capSpentMicros.description: What the run's spend ceiling (budget.usdMicros) has counted against it, across its segments, including calls that failed after they were sent (counted at their worst case).

tainted.description: Untrusted content entered the run (Warden said so, or a call to a tool that returns outside text went through); a resumed segment starts tainted.

inheritedTaint.description: The run started tainted because of what an earlier run of the task left: a last summary written by a tainted run, or a folder a tainted run wrote to.

taintSeal.description: HMAC, under the home's Warden key, of the fields that decide the run's taint (`trigger`, `input`, `tainted`, `inheritedTaint`). Missing or wrong: the run is read as tainted.

sideEffects.description: How many state-changing calls the run recorded.

approvals.description: Approvals the run asked for, across its segments (budget.maxApprovals).

approvalWaitMs.description: Time the run spent waiting for approvals, across its segments (budget.approvalWaitMs).

type.description: tool_call | tool_result | replayed | denied | info | error | resume | approval

confirmEnvelope.description: With `enabled: true`: confirm the envelope as a pre-approval. Must equal the task's current `confirmation.digest` after this request's own edits (409 `confirmation_mismatch` otherwise, and nothing changes). Accepted only from a caller who may answer approvals (the loopback owner or a signed-in session; 403 `trusted_local_confirmation_required`) in a same-origin request. Without it, enabling leaves the envelope a restriction.

id.description: Stable notice id; a client that has shown it must not show it again.

text.description: The card as stored in the conversation.

from.description: Always "Lisa" — the reach-out gate stamps every proactive message.

reachOutId.description: Reach-out ledger id; pass it to POST /api/reachout/feedback. The gate also emits an idle_message (source task|watcher) carrying the same id.

TaskResultEvent.description: A task result the reach-out gate let through. The same result is stored as a card in the conversation.

kind.description: approval or handoff. A handoff cannot be approved, only dismissed.

digest.description: The digest of the payload the approver was shown (from GET /api/approvals/{id}). Required; a missing or stale digest is refused.

origins.description: Where each LOOSENING rule applies, by map and key, e.g. {"tools": {"bash": ["chat", "task"]}}. A rule that loosens (auto, or less strict than the default it replaces) applies to the attended chat only unless its scope names `task`; a rule that tightens applies to every origin. Every entry must name an existing rule.

Open set; v1 values: read, self, draft, write, exec, network, send, publish, purchase, delete, credential.

scope.description: Open set; v1 values: once, task, target, 24h, always.

value.description: The whole value, secrets masked, never clipped.

primary.description: Shown first: the field that says what the call does.

fields.description: Every field of the tool input, in the server's order (primary fields first).

userCode.description: Short-lived GitHub device user code. No access token.

GitHubConnectionChangedEvent.description: Invalidation only; fetch the local-owner card endpoint. Clients ignore unknown events.

name.description: Linear account display name; stable id remains the identity key.

authorizationUrl.description: Short-lived trusted Google or Linear authorization URL; no access token or PKCE verifier.

corrupt.description: Not clean UTF-8; edits are refused (409) until repaired.

query.description: At least 3 characters, or 2 when it contains a Chinese, Japanese or Korean character (whitespace collapsed); at most 200.

dryRun.description: true previews; anything else applies and needs digest.

digest.description: The digest of the confirmed preview. Required to apply.

id.description: Stable item id; apply changes only previewed ids.

location.description: Home-relative path; memory entries as path#id, transcript and soul-file lines as path:line.

snippet.description: Dry run only: about 80 characters of text around the first match.

why.description: Why this action, e.g. title, tag, file name.

digest.description: Digest of the previewed item ids; pass back to apply.

counts.description: Matches per layer: memory, user, kb, memory_kb_links, sessions, reflections, tasks, connectors, reve, search_index, relationships, journal. search_index is non-zero only when another layer is.

scanned.description: Areas forget searches and an applied forget re-scans, as 'area — what'.

notScanned.description: Entries present in this home that can hold user text and are not scanned, as 'path — what'; each is also a 'Not scanned: …' residual.

remaining.description: Apply only: matches per layer found by a re-scan of the scanned areas after the writes. Says nothing about notScanned.

corrupt.description: Ids of records that exist but could not be parsed.

path.description: Relative to the caller's home, POSIX separators.

notRevertibleReason.description: Why a user-part change cannot be reverted, when it cannot.

capped.description: A snapshot cap was hit: a part left out, or some file's content not kept.

uncaptured.description: Parts the capture left out whole (over the file cap); their changes are not listed.

skippedSymlinks.description: Symlinks met where a tracked file or directory would be; never followed (first 50).

readTruncated.description: The stored record is over the 512 KiB cap; this view was trimmed (diffs first) to fit.

status.description: pending: waiting for a pass; claimed: shown to a pass that is still running; delivered: acknowledged by a pass that finished.

deliveredIn.description: Dream id of the pass that received the note and finished.

claimedIn.description: While claimed: the dream id of the running pass.

changedSince.description: Memory files among `reverted` that no longer held exactly what the dream left. Their entries were reverted against the current text; an entry the dream removed was put back even if a later edit had replaced it. A warning, not a refusal.

reason.description: modified_since: changed after the dream (KB / skills); not_revertible: no pre-dream copy, or one that does not match the record, or the file was also changed outside the pass while it ran; unsafe_target: the path resolves outside its part's directory (a symlink on the way, or the file is one); memory_full: the reverted MEMORY.md / USER.md would be larger than the memory store's cap (4096 / 2048 bytes). force overrides modified_since and skips not_revertible / unsafe_target files; memory_full is refused even with force, and nothing is written.

id.description: First 16 bytes of SHA-256(raw X25519 public key), lowercase hex.
